summary.text: Rob Woodward is the Republican candidate for Colorado State Senate District 15 in the November 3, 2026 general election, against incumbent Democrat Janice Marchman.
He previously represented District 15 in the Colorado State Senate from January 2019 to January 2023.

paragraphs.text: Rob Woodward graduated from Colorado State University in 1990, then moved to Chicago to work in corporate finance while earning an M.B.A.
He later moved to New York to help launch an investment banking company and returned to Colorado in 1995.
Woodward was elected to the Colorado State Senate in 2018, succeeding Kevin Lundberg, and took office on January 4, 2019.
In 2019 and 2020 he served on the Senate Finance Committee, the Colorado Health Insurance Exchange Oversight Committee and the Statutory Revision Committee, of which he was vice chair.
In 2021 and 2022 he was assigned to the Legislative Audit Committee, the Statutory Revision Committee and the Business, Labor, and Technology Committee.
He left office on January 9, 2023, and Janice Marchman succeeded him.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Woodward described his background as being in small business and entrepreneurship and said he and his wife, Paula, have three children.
He listed affordability, an all-of-the-above approach to energy that includes oil and gas as well as wind, solar and geothermal, and public safety as campaign priorities.
